content: Doxylamine succinate is an antihistamine that has been approved by the FDA for the treatment of allergic rhinitis, the common cold, and insomnia. A common adverse reaction associated with its use is drowsiness. For adults, the FDA-labeled indication for doxylamine succinate is as a nighttime sleep aid. The recommended dosage is one tablet taken 30 minutes before bedtime, once daily, or as directed by a physician. There is limited information available regarding off-label uses of doxylamine succinate in adults, whether supported by guidelines or not. For pediatric patients, the FDA-labeled indication is also as a nighttime sleep aid. For children aged 12 years and older, the dosage is one tablet taken 30 minutes before bedtime, once daily, or as directed by a physician. Doxylamine succinate should not be used in children under 12 years of age. There is limited information regarding off-label uses of doxylamine succinate in pediatric patients, whether supported by guidelines or not. Doxylamine succinate is contraindicated in children under 12 years of age. Patients with breathing problems such as asthma, emphysema, or chronic bronchitis; glaucoma; or difficulty urinating due to an enlarged prostate gland should consult a doctor before use. Additionally, individuals taking other medications should consult a doctor or pharmacist before using this product. Alcoholic beverages should be avoided while using this medication, and it should only be taken at bedtime. If sleeplessness persists for more than two weeks, discontinue use and consult a doctor, as insomnia may be a symptom of a more serious underlying medical condition. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult a healthcare professional before use. In case of overdose, seek immediate medical attention or contact a Poison Control Center. There is limited information available regarding clinical trial experience, postmarketing experience, drug interactions, and contraindications for doxylamine succinate in the drug label. Similarly, there is no FDA guidance on its use during pregnancy, labor and delivery, nursing, pediatric use, geriatric use, or in specific populations such as those with renal or hepatic impairment, immunocompromised patients, or specific gender or racial groups. Doxylamine succinate is administered orally. There is limited information regarding its monitoring, IV compatibility, chronic overdose, mechanism of action, structure, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, nonclinical toxicology, clinical studies, and storage in the drug label. Patients should be counseled to avoid alcohol while taking doxylamine succinate, as the interaction between alcohol and this medication has not been established. Patients should discuss the potential effects of alcohol consumption with their doctor. Doxylamine succinate is marketed under brand names such as 7 Select Sleep Aid and Unisom. There is limited information regarding look-alike drug names in the drug label.
